texts.body: It is 6:40 and the kitchen is still blue. I am out the back door before the kettle boils, and I run the towpath as far as the second bridge. Sam is still asleep. I am the kind of person who does the boring thing on the ordinary Tuesday. The phone stays in the hall after ten.
The alarm goes and I turn it off. The kitchen is still blue but I am not in it. The towpath is somewhere I used to go. Sam stopped asking.

letters.body: I have been reading what you wrote, the night you wrote it. You wrote “It is 6:40 and the kitchen is still blue.” and I have thought about that line more than you did. The ledger is still empty, which is the ordinary state of a thing that has just begun. None of it was the day you felt like it. That is the part nobody tells you: the feeling arrives afterwards, if it arrives at all, and the work goes first either way. I am not writing to tell you it gets easier. I am writing because somebody should have a record of the mornings you did it anyway, and it turns out that somebody is you, later. Start with the smallest thing tomorrow. I will keep the rest of it safe until you need it.
